name: Today
kid: A thin glass thread brings the internet into the house as flashes of light, fast enough for everyone at home to watch videos at once.
nerd: Fibre to the home or to the building: GPON or XGS-PON (gigabits, shared by a neighbourhood), or Ethernet from the basement. Wi‑Fi 6 and NAT at home.

describe.kid: A phone in your hand. It’s on Wi‑Fi to the router, and the router has a glass thread to the internet.
describe.nerd: A smartphone on Wi‑Fi 6 behind a home router, with fibre, or a cable from the basement, as its uplink.

on-the-go.kid: Out on the street, phones are on 5G: radio to a cell tower nearby, then a glass thread to the internet. Fast enough for big videos.
on-the-go.nerd: 5G NR: wide carriers and many antennas give a phone tens to hundreds of Mbit/s. The gNB tunnels the packets (GTP-U) over fibre to the core’s UPF.

describe.kid: A phone in your hand, out on the street, on 5G to a cell tower.
describe.nerd: A smartphone on 5G NR to a gNB, with fibre backhaul to the mobile core.

describe.kid: A laptop on the desk, with a cable to the router, and the router has a glass thread to the internet.
describe.nerd: A laptop on Ethernet to the home router, with fibre (XGS-PON) as its uplink.
